Topline: inbound from content marketing platform -> looking to consolidate generation pipeline into single hosted API.

Discovery summary: trialing several provider APIs; primary motivations are throughput and per-token cost control. High-volume use (daily batch jobs + on-demand marketing emails). Very interested in automatic caching and batching to reduce per-token spend.

Key quotes from discovery call: "We generate thousands of articles and email variants per week — unit cost matters more than bleeding-edge quality." 

Workload details: mostly bulk generation (long-form articles 600-1,800 words), template-based email personalization (short chat-like prompts), and multi-locale content transforms. Typical request sizes: 700-4,000 tokens for articles, 50-300 tokens for emails. Peak concurrent requests during nightly batch window: ~300 requests; steady-state API calls per minute during business hours: ~60-120.

SLOs & constraints: target 95th p95 token latency <200ms for short requests (email renders), flexible for long-form where batch throughput is prioritized. Cost sensitivity: target effective per-1k-token cost under $0.40 for long-form after caching/quantization. Preference to use smaller open models for high-volume drafts with an option to route final quality pass to a stronger model.

Security/compliance: company uses SSO (Okta), requires audit logging for API usage and request metadata; no strict data residency—public cloud ok. Interested in KMS for encryption-in-transit storage of customer prompt templates but lower priority.

Technical asks: demo of Redwood hosted API, examples of batching config and prefix caching, recommended model profiles (quantized variants), guidance on token accounting for templated prompts. Wants example pricing calc for 1M tokens/day.
